=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9065-9078 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The integration judge posts its diagnosis and resolution guidance as a tracking-issue comment, but the dispatched resolver does not receive that comment in its prompt.
  WHY: The resolver uses the tracking issue title and body, not the judge’s comment, so it retries conflict resolution without the guidance.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9048-9083, 10853-10865 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The active-resolver check occurs after the integration judge runs and posts its diagnosis, and the caller leaves `unresolved_ticks` at the escalation threshold.
  WHY: Each poll tick while a resolver is active can run the judge again and post another tracking-issue comment before discovering the active resolver.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22113 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The RB_JUDGE callsite checks for exit code 75 even though `poller_judge_isolated` converts sandbox-helper-outdated 75 returns to 77 before returning.
  WHY: The 75 check is currently dead code; the source notes it is harmless unless a raw-75 return path is reintroduced.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  confidence=[5]

  EVIDENCE: The judge posts resolution guidance as a tracking-issue comment, but the resolver prompt reads the tracking issue title and body, not comments; scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:631-638; the dispatched workflow builds a fresh prompt with no knowledge of the judge’s diagnosis.
- requirement: “If one is already in flight, the judge defers without charging another dispatch against the integration branch's lifetime budget.”
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh near line 9048 or the caller at line 10853
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The active-resolver guard runs after the judge completes and posts its comment; the caller defers without consuming budget, but `unresolved_ticks` is not reset, so the next poll tick re-invokes the judge.
- requirement: The orchestrator judge should dispatch the “unchanged codex command” when a poller judge resolves to Codex or Claude is unavailable (Phase 5c plan).
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh::poller_judge_isolated and the five poller judge call sites
  confidence=[5]

  EVIDENCE: `poller_judge_isolated` routes the fallback through `_poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt`, which invokes `review_untrusted_sandbox.sh`; the prior direct Codex command is not retained. z-ai_glm-5_2 reports this implementation is intentional and documented, and that the PR description wording is imprecise rather than a task gap.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 9065-9071 (guidance posting) and review_conflict_prepare.sh:631-638 (resolver context) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The integration judge posts resolution_guidance only as a tracking-issue comment, but the resolver receives only the tracking-issue title and body (capped at 4000 bytes), not the comments.
  WHY: The resolver prompt is assembled from PR metadata (review_conflict_prepare.sh:631-638 reads INTEGRATION_TRACKING_TITLE and INTEGRATION_TRACKING_BODY). The judge's diagnosis comment on the tracking issue is not fetched as PR comment context.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 9078-9083 (dispatch after judge) and 10853-10865 (caller's return-3 handling) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The integration judge runs before checking whether a resolver is already in-flight, and the return-3 path does not reset `integration_conflict_unresolved_ticks`.
  WHY: On the next poll tick, unresolved_ticks still meets the threshold, triggering another judge invocation and another duplicate tracking-issue comment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 22113 (RB_JUDGE exit-code check) and poller_judge_isolated (return conversion at ~231-235) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The RB_JUDGE callsite checks for both exit code 77 and 75, but poller_judge_isolated converts all sandbox-helper-outdated 75 returns to 77 before returning.
  WHY: This is a dead-code observation, not a runtime failure. If a future change reintroduced a raw-75 return path from poller_claude_judge, the check would become live again. Currently harmless.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "The integration judge returns a bounded diagnosis; deterministic poller code re-dispatches the existing isolated conflict resolver." (README.md:2109-2110)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh::invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict
  Evidence of absence: The judge posts resolution guidance as a tracking-issue comment, but the dispatched resolver never receives it. The resolver prompt (review_conflict_prepare.sh:631-638) reads only the tracking issue title and body, not comments. The "bounded diagnosis" is therefore produced but wasted—it never reaches the component that would use it.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "If one is already in flight, the judge defers without charging another dispatch against the integration branch's lifetime budget." (README.md:2110-2111)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh near line 9048 or the caller at line 10853
  Evidence of absence: The active-resolver guard inside _dispatch_review_for_conflicts runs only after the judge completes and posts its comment. When the dispatch discovers the resolver is active and returns exit 2, invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict returns 3. The caller at 10856-10858 defers without consuming budget, but unresolved_ticks is not reset. The next poll tick re-invokes the judge and posts another comment. There is no pre-dispatch active-resolver check, and no per-cycle deduplication of the judge invocation when the resolver is already in-flight.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 9065-9078 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The integration judge’s resolution guidance is not received by the review resolver.
  WHY: The resolver prompt receives the tracking issue title and body, but not the comments. The PR review metadata collector fetches comments for the PR number, not the tracking issue.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 9048, 9067-9079, 10853-10865 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The active-resolver check occurs after the integration judge runs, causing redundant judge calls and duplicated comments.
  WHY: Each poll tick reaches the judge before checking if a resolver is already active. Since `post_tracking_comment` performs a POST, it produces duplicated comments on the tracking issue, leading to noise and API overhead.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The orchestrator judge should dispatch the “unchanged codex command” when a poller judge resolves to Codex or Claude is unavailable (Phase 5c plan).
  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh::poller_judge_isolated` and the five poller judge call sites
  Evidence of absence: The logic in `poller_judge_isolated` currently routes all failures through `_poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt`, which invokes `review_untrusted_sandbox.sh`. The prior direct `codex` invocation pattern is not retained as a fallback for the isolated judge; the implementation replaces it with a hard-coded sandbox execution, which deviates from the specified "unchanged codex command" fallback behavior.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The integration judge must pass its resolution_guidance and diagnosis to the resolver it dispatches, so the resolver can use the judge's diagnosis when reconciling conflicts.
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9065-9078 (post-judge dispatch block) and scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh (resolver prompt builder)
  Evidence of absence: The new integration judge in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9063-9078 HTML-escapes the diagnosis/resolution_guidance and posts them as a tracking-issue comment, then calls _dispatch_review_for_conflicts to re-run the existing resolver. The resolver prompt built by scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:631-638 is assembled from PR metadata (PR body, title, files, intent fingerprints), not from tracking-issue comments. There is no path that carries the judge verdict to the resolver's input. The dispatch fires workflow_dispatch on review_autofix.yml, which will build a fresh prompt with no knowledge of the judge's diagnosis. The judge is therefore an expensive model call whose primary output is discarded.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The poller should detect that a resolver is already in flight on the integration PR head BEFORE running the integration judge, and defer the entire tick without a model call.
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh heal_integration_branch_conflict (~line 10851) and the entry into invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict
  Evidence of absence: The current flow at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10851-10858 invokes invoke_judge_for_integration_conflict unconditionally whenever unresolved_ticks >= effective_max_retries. The active-resolver detection (return code 3) only fires AFTER the judge model has already executed and AFTER the judge has called _dispatch_review_for_conflicts. Each poll tick that finds an active resolver therefore incurs a full integration-judge model call AND posts a new tracking-issue comment ("## Integration conflict diagnosis") via post_tracking_comment, which performs an unduplicated POST. The new deferral path at :10854-10857 catches the 3 return code but only after paying the model cost. The fix is to call _has_active_autofix_run (or the equivalent from the poller's existing preflight, which already detects active review runs on the same head) before invoking the judge and return 0 immediately, mirroring the existing build_active_issue_set / _has_active_autofix_run patterns elsewhere in the same file.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The PR description states poller judges' Claude-exit-75 fallback runs "its unchanged codex/OpenCode command"—that is, the same model path the role used before Phase 5c.
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh poller_judge_isolated (the post-75 retry) and the description text
  Evidence of absence: The poller judges previously invoked bash ${ORCH_CODEX_ISOLATED_EXEC} run --mode read-only ... for the codex model. The new poller_judge_isolated at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:248-260 routes the Claude-exit-75 retry through _poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt codex, which writes an OpenCode configuration (write_opencode_config.sh --role writer) and runs opencode via review_untrusted_sandbox.sh.
